title: Selectors, Declarations, and Rules
summary: Target the right elements with type, class, and descendant selectors, then build valid declaration blocks from properties and values.

sketchBlocks.title: A rule combines a selector with declarations
Type selectors are broad; class selectors are reusable and specific
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
A **type selector** such as `p` targets every matching element of that type. That is useful when you want a site-wide baseline. A **class selector** starts with a dot and targets elements whose HTML `class` attribute contains that class: ```css .intro { font-size: 1.2rem; } ``` ```html

Aspiring web developer.

``` Classes are reusable. Several elements can share the same class, and one element can carry multiple classes. Use a class when the styling represents a reusable role or component rather than every element of one HTML type.

options: A p selector can apply one rule to paragraph elements across the linked pages.

quizDraft.title: Use a type selector across the portfolio
quizDraft.prompt:
## CSS task

The shared stylesheet is connected, but paragraph text still relies on the browser's default foreground `color`. A type selector is appropriate when the same visual decision should apply to every element of one semantic type. Continue from the stylesheet created in the previous topic. In `styles.css`, use a type selector to set every `p` element to `color: #334155;`. Preview multiple pages; do not rewrite the inherited HTML. Preview Home, About, and Projects: paragraph copy should share the same calmer slate `color` without any HTML changes.

### File to edit

`styles.css`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on.
quizDraft.hint: Target the paragraph element name directly and keep the earlier h1 rule.

quizDraft.title: Use the portfolio's small class hook
quizDraft.prompt:
## CSS task

The Home introduction now shares the paragraph `color`, but it needs a little more emphasis than ordinary body copy. The existing intro class gives you a focused styling hook without making every paragraph heavier. Keep all previous CSS. The inherited Home-page introduction has the one CSS-course hook `class="intro"`. Use `.intro` to set `font-weight: 600;`. Do not add more classes just to solve this exercise. Check Home: the introduction should read more prominently while ordinary paragraphs on all pages keep their normal weight.

### File to edit

`styles.css`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on.
quizDraft.hint: Use the class hook that is already present; do not add new classes just for this task.

quizDraft.title: Use a descendant selector for navigation links
quizDraft.prompt:
## CSS task

Navigation works on every page, but its links still look like unrelated default links. A descendant selector can style only anchors inside navigation without adding a class to every link. Keep the cumulative stylesheet. Use the descendant selector `nav a` to set navigation links to `color: #0f766e;`. Preview Home, About, Projects, and Contact to see the shared selector work. Preview multiple pages: navigation links should share the teal accent while links outside nav remain governed by their own styles.

### File to edit

`styles.css`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on.
quizDraft.hint: Describe the relationship between the nav ancestor and its anchor descendants.

help.concept: A descendant selector can style only anchors inside navigation without adding a class to every link.
help.hint_1: Describe the relationship between the nav ancestor and its anchor descendants.
help.hint_2: Preview multiple pages: navigation links should share the teal accent while links outside nav remain governed by their own styles.
